basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 29.' and it opens 'Vers. 29. Cui pater Balam servam tradiderat. Liae data fuerat ancilla superius nomine'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 29. Cui pater Balam servam tradiderat. Liae data fuerat ancilla superius nomine Zelpha, Racheli vero data Bala nomine. Zelpha interpretatur os loquens; Bala, inveterata. Significant hae duae ancillae eos qui vel in activa vita vel in contemplativa non recta intentione bona operantur, nec recto studio | praedicant, id est non pro Deo, sed pro favore aut commodis saeculi; de qualibus Apostolus dicit: Sunt, qui praedicant Christum non sincere (Philip. I, 1). Et post pauca: Utrum ex occasione, an pro veritate Christus annuntietur, in hoc gaudeo, sed et gaudebo (Ibid., 18). Unde recte Zelpha os loquens interpretatur, quia tales in ore habent praedicationes, non in corde, de quibus dicitur: Populus hic labiis me honorat, cor autem eorum longe est a me (Matth. XV, 8). Bala autem inveterata dicitur, quia tales, licet bonorum operum fructus quasi bonos filios afferant, tamen quia non recto studio hoc agunt, adhuc in veteris erroris conversatione perdurant.
